source: Bank for International Settlements, locational banking statistics (WS_LBS_D_PUB), key Q.S.C.A.USD.A.5J.A.5A.A.<counterparty>.N: cross-border claims of all reporting countries' banks, all instruments, US dollars; 5J = all counterparties
note: Cross-border claims are what banks in one country are owed by borrowers in other countries: loans, deposits and debt securities, in every currency, converted to US dollars by the BIS. A country is where the lending bank's office is, not the nationality of the bank, so a Japanese bank's London branch counts as the United Kingdom. Financial centres such as the Cayman Islands book loans for banking groups based elsewhere. The BIS counts claims on other banks and on offices of the same bank too, so this is not all credit to companies and households. The amounts are claims in US dollars, shown in US dollars. Not assigned is claims the BIS places on no country. Source: Bank for International Settlements.
